data.body: Today `ddflow next --phase P-perf-metrics` returns only the READY items that live INSIDE that phase. A phase at the tail of the critical path (P-perf-metrics) then shows '0 ready / 21 blocked' with no way to see — from the same command — which upstream dependencies are themselves ready to claim. Feature: by default `ddflow next --phase <id>` should ALSO include the phase's unmet dependencies' ready items (so a lane asked to drive a phase can start the upstream blockers first); an explicit parameter (e.g. `--phase-only` / `--no-deps` / `--scope phase`) restores the current in-phase-only behaviour. The default must not disguise the phase boundary: label each returned upstream item as a blocking-dependency, not an in-phase item.
data.title: ddflow next --phase <id> returns only in-phase ready items, hiding the ready upstream dependencies that block the phase

evidence.note: Falsifiable claim: a lane agent whose measured context is below [session].agent_rotate_tokens (250000) produces NO rotate hint, and one at/above it does; the hint names finishing the item, writing a hand-off note into the item's evidence and stopping, then a fresh agent from ddflow brief. Probe (cheapest test): tests/test_lane_rotate.py run against the worktree code -- test_hint_is_silent_below_the_threshold and test_hint_fires_at_the_threshold_from_fixture_usage pass (249999 -> '', 250000 -> 'rotate ... ddflow brief'). Refuter per TE-context-caps: rotated lanes need MORE review rounds/rework vs un-rotated (ddflow metrics, 20 items each). Mechanism (research 3.3): 12 agents with 300+ calls = 67% of subagent spend, 39 over 200K; past the threshold a growing context, not more work, dominates cost.

Applied governing rules: r-everything-configurable (threshold + window as [session] knobs), r-bounded-everything (HANDOFF_NOTE_CHARS cap, hint silent when unknown), r-evidence-over-assertion (hint fires only on a measured usage, never a guess), r-docs-with-the-change (driver delta names CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW/CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE). r-gemini-key-load honoured before reviews.

Implemented in worktree branch ddflow/TE-context-caps: ddflow/services/lanerotate.py (hint/rotating/handoff_note/window_env/doctor_notes/brief_hint), [session] knobs agent_rotate_tokens=250000 + claude_autocompact_window + claude_autocompact_pct_override (ddflow/config_sections/session.py), doctor wiring (api/reporting/health.py), wake-brief wiring (api/lifecycle/brief.py), driver delta (docs/ddflow/drivers/deltas/claude-code.md). tests/test_lane_rotate.py: 13 passed (ruff clean).

chunk_findings.detail: The knob documents a Claude Code range of 100000-1000000, with 0 meaning "leave the harness default", but `check=int_at_least(0)` accepts every other non-negative integer. Config `claude_autocompact_window=1` (or `2000000`) therefore loads, and doctor/health will name `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` at a value Claude Code's own range rejects, so the D-TE-Q2 alternative to rotation never actually compact the session.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/session.py:claude_autocompact_window

chunk_findings.detail: `handoff_note` claims the whole note is capped at `HANDOFF_NOTE_CHARS` (400), but the cap is applied only to the summary and the ellipsis is added outside the remaining budget. With `item_id="x"*359` (so `len(prefix)+len(suffix)==400`), any summary yields `budget==0` and the return value is 401 characters (`"…"` is still appended). With `item_id="x"*400`, `budget` is negative, the body collapses to `"…"`, and the note is 412+ characters and still ends with the suffix, so a 400-character brief paste drops `"; resume with \`ddflow brief\`."`.

chunk_findings.detail: `handoff_note` does not keep a bounded note that still ends with the resume suffix once the id is long. `room` is `max(400 - len(prefix) - len(suffix), 0)`, so an `item_id` of 400 characters makes `prefix` alone longer than `HANDOFF_NOTE_CHARS`, `room` is 0, and the function still appends `"…"` plus `"; resume with \`ddflow brief\`."` and then returns `note[:400]`. That slice cuts the suffix (and can cut the id), so the note the lead is supposed to paste into `ddflow brief` no longer contains the resume instruction the cap was meant to preserve.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanerotate.py:handoff_note
